newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power in US$560 mln China power plant JV.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power in US$560 mln China power plant JV.

text.p: Singapore Power, United Engineers Ltd and the Government of Singapore Investment Corp (GIC) said on Monday they would partner a Chinese consortium to build a US$560 million power plant in China's Anhui Province.
Singapore Power said in a statement the Singapore partners would hold a 49 percent stake in the project to build the 700MW (mega watt) plant.
The Singapore stake would be held by a company called United Power Corp Pte Ltd in which Singapore Power would have a 33 percent equity interest.
The remaining 67 percent would be held by United Infrastructure Pte Ltd, a joint venture of United Engineers and the GIC.
Four Chinese firms would hold a controlling 51 percent stake in the power plant.

East China Power Group would hold 20 percent, Anhui Electric Power Development Company would take 16 percent, while 7.5 percent would be held by Anhui Electric Power Company and Hefei Construction & Investment Company, the statement said.
The plant, consisting of two 350MW coal-fired power generators, is expected to be operational by the end of 2000.
Funding for the project would be a mix of equity finance of about US$144 million with the rest coming from project finance, the statement said.
